newsitem.title: USA: U.S. offers compromise over Helms-Burton Act - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. offers compromise over Helms-Burton Act - report.

text.p: In an effort to avert a trade dispute with the European Union, the Clinton administration is offering to seek modification of the Helms-Burton Act in exchange for European efforts to discourage some types of investment in Cuba, the Washington Post reported on Friday.
The newspaper said the deal calls for the European Union to suspend for six months its complaint against the United States in the World Trade Organisation.
Senior administration officials had begun briefing key members of Congress on the proposed deal, the Post added.

The plan calls for the Europeans to "establish disciplines to deter" private companies in Europe from investing in property confiscated without compensation, not just in Cuba but globally, according to the report.
In exchange, Congress would be asked to relax some provisions of Helms-Burton, the U.S. law that imposes sanctions on foreign companies that "traffic" in confisctaed property in Cuba.
The European Union, which strongly opposes the law as an unjustifiable effort by the United States to impose its anti-Cuban policies on others, has filed a formal complaint with the WTO.

The Clinton administration has said the WTO does not have jurisdiction because the matter is not a trade dispute but a national security issue and has called on the Europeans to withdraw their complaint.
